featured_reviews.review_text:
This Lucknowi chicken biryani was a standout. The flavors were perfectly balanced, with a good level of spiciness that wasn't overpowering. The chicken was incredibly tender and cooked to perfection, and the rice was fluffy and aromatic, with each grain perfectly infused with the spices.
The dish had a generous amount of chicken pieces and was topped with crispy, caramelized onions, which added a wonderful sweet crunch and texture. It was served with a side of cooling raita, which complemented the richness of the biryani beautifully.
The portion size was ample, definitely enough to be a satisfying meal. For an authentic and truly delicious biryani experience, this is a must-try, especially if you appreciate the classic Lucknowi style.

featured_reviews.name: melanie pais
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kerala Kitchen & Bar is hands down one of the most delightful dining experiences I’ve had in a long time.

From the very first sip to the last bite, everything was exceptional—the drinks were refreshing, the milkshakes indulgent, and every course that followed just kept getting better. The starters were packed with authentic flavours, the main course was rich and comforting, and the desserts were the perfect sweet ending. Truly, some of the best Kerala cuisine I’ve ever tasted.
What makes this place even more special is the ambience—it genuinely transports you to Kerala. Serene, beautiful, and thoughtfully designed, it creates a calming escape right in the middle of Juhu.
The staff deserves a special mention—warm, attentive, and incredibly kind, they make you feel right at home. It’s also wonderfully kid-friendly, making it perfect for family outings.
This is not just a one-time visit kind of place—I’ll definitely be coming back with family and friends. If you love great food, great vibes, and heartfelt hospitality, this one is an absolute must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Umesh Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great place, the moment you enter this Resturant you get a different and pleasant feel. We being vegetarian, ordered all veg food, started with Rasam Soup followed by Neer Dosa, Set Dosa, Persactu Dosa,Thate Idli and
papaya-Paysam. Every items were tasty we enjoyed thoroughly. The service was very quick, the entire team serving all the tables were excellent , the place is very clean. Best part is the food is very light and has good after taste as well.
We advise them to have veg and non-veg sitting arrangement separate so vegetarians are comfortable. The first half from entrance gate should be offered to vegetarian/Veg section and one after that should be non veg section.
Over all it’s an excellent place and would love to visit this place again

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
New place in juhu we decided to visit on a whim. The chemmeen cheriya ulli perattu is a perfect starter that's goes with parotta, only problem is that the parotta was not good. Very flat barely any fluff or flakes in it.
The kanava crispy fry was a let down, it's just fried squid with no flavour.  They didn't give us any dips or chutney with it.
Chemmeen manga curry was the hero of the afternoon. Tasty, tangy, full of prawns and raw mango. What's not to like. We paired them with freshly made appams and neer dosa.
The seafood biryani wasn't bad either, good flavour and full of prawns and squid.

The service was decent but it was disappointing to see that they served every table with fryuns and chutney but not us.  It's a small thing but it still is weird.
Still, I'm definitely going back again to try some of their other items.

featured_reviews.name: Al J
featured_reviews.review_text: Fantastic North Indian Feast at Copper Chimney, Juhu. We had an unforgettable dinner at Copper Chimney in Juhu – authentic, flavorful, and perfectly atomistic in every bite! The mixed grill was a star, juicy and smoky with an array of chutneys that added zesty punches of flavor. Paired with fluffy rumali rotis, buttery tandoori naan, and creamy paneer kurchan, it was pure indulgence. We sipped on refreshing Mumbai Mustani mocktails, and ended with the decadent Peshawari kulfi for dessert. The lively atmosphere was elevated by the attentive and friendly staff( Dave our server) , who made our evening seamless. Amazing food, drinks, and service all around – a must-visit for Mumbai foodies!

featured_reviews.name: Tina Wa
featured_reviews.review_text: Wow the food here is exceptional. I’m a female travelling solo for work and really enjoyed eating here. I had the veggie biryani and the dal. The portion was about 3x more than I could eat, and believe me, I tried! Amazing.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Really sweet staff that will recommend what's best if you are confused with the extensive menu. I'm reviewing a while after I went so I have forgotten the names of the dishes but I'll try to keep it clear.
The gosht dum biryani was an absolute disappointment, for the price point the flavour was abysmal. It tasted just like lightly spiced rice with some meat. Not at all what to expect from a nice place like this.
The chicken tikka we had was lovely, super soft and delicious, paired perfectly with our beers.
The rumali roti and naan were also very good, soft and tasty. Cannot complain.
The main course I believe we had the murg rahra that we licked clean. Rich and tasty.
Definitely going back here again for the curries and kebabs. Skipping all rice items, total scam.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I attended the currently ongoing  "Phulkari" event by Copper chimney a meticulously crafted, flavourful and colorful menu inspired by Phulkari. Phulkari, after all, is more than just an art; it symbolizes tradition, joy, and togetherness....the very spirit of Diwali.

Foods on the menu that are a must try-
✨ Rose rumali roti with a creamy and flavourful walnut malai dip- A crisp rumali roti with subtle hints of rose teams with a creamy mellow walnutty dip.
✨ Chukandar Tikki with Missi Roti: The absolute melt in the mouth " Chukandar Tikki" with Missi Roti made me think....Who knew beetroot could taste so good 😅
✨Tandoori Pineapple- Smoky, spiced and my personal favourite.(....yes, I am biased when it comes to spiced pineapple😅)

And if you have a sweet tooth....

✨ Mava gujiya: A classic and must have.
✨ Badam halwa with malai ice cream: Rich, creamy and  definitely not for the faint hearted 😅

Drinks:
✨ Phoolkari- A subtle and soothing drink inspired by Bagh phulkari
✨ Anar Da Bagh- Another beautifully crafted drink inspired by Bagh Phulkari

Overall, Phulkari by Copper Chimney feels like a cultural celebration on a plate through flavor, color, and creativity.

From the moment we entered, the ambience felt warm, elegant, and perfect for a professional yet relaxed meeting setup. The staff was extremely courteous, attentive, and ensured everything was handled smoothly throughout the evening.

The food quality was outstanding. The kebabs were perfectly cooked, flavourful, and served beautifully. The Dal Qureshi and biryani were exceptional and easily among the best dishes we tried that evening. What stood out most was the balance in flavours — rich yet not overpowering. Even the presentation and serving style reflected the premium dining experience the restaurant is known for.

The environment was calm enough for meaningful business conversations while still carrying a luxurious fine-dining vibe. Service timing, food recommendations, and hospitality were all top-notch.

Overall, it was a memorable experience and definitely a place I would recommend for both family dining and corporate meetings. Looking forward to visiting again soon.

featured_reviews.name: The Beekeeper
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Tanatan near Juhu Beach on Christmas Eve for lunch. The first thing that stands out about the place is its beautiful interiors — they are quite impressive and give off a royal, grand kind of vibe. The ambience definitely adds to the overall dining experience. They also had live music during the daytime, which created a pleasant and lively atmosphere.

The service, however, was average. The staff was polite, but the food preparation and service took longer than expected, so you might have to wait a bit for your order to arrive at the table.

In terms of food, I ordered the tandoori chicken. Unfortunately, it wasn’t the best experience. The chicken was slightly burnt on the sides and, considering the price, the portion size and quality didn’t really justify the cost. The place felt a bit on the expensive side overall.

I’m rating this place 3 stars mainly because of the ambience and the overall experience the restaurant offers. However, the food quality and pricing could definitely be improved to match the premium feel of the place.

featured_reviews.name: Dheeraj Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful dining experience here. The ambience is beautiful with warm interiors, comfortable seating, and live music that made the evening even more enjoyable. We started with the Peeli Mirch Ke Wings and Kozhi Ghee Roast, both packed with flavour and cooked perfectly. The wings had the right balance of spice, while the ghee roast was rich and aromatic.
For the mains, the Sunny Side Up Appam with Chicken Sukhna was a unique combination and easily my favourite dish of the night. The Chicken Tikka Biryani was flavourful with tender pieces of chicken and well-cooked rice. Paired everything with the refreshing Thanda Teekha Mocktail and ended on a sweet note with the indulgent Killer KitKat Freakshake. Great food, great vibe, and excellent service. Highly recommended!

Had a wonderful dining experience at Tanatan Juhu, especially with their limited-time Mango Menu, which is currently live. We started with the Mango Colada, a refreshing tropical drink with the perfect balance of sweetness and mango flavor. For dessert, the fresh mango chunks served with vanilla ice cream were simple yet incredibly satisfying, making the most of the season's best fruit.

Among the starters, the Hara Bhara Tikke stood out with its crisp exterior and flavorful, well-seasoned filling. The Paneer Tikka was equally impressive—soft, smoky, and marinated beautifully with rich spices. For the main course, we opted for the biryani, which was aromatic, flavorful, and cooked to perfection with well-balanced spices.

The food, presentation, and overall ambiance made for a memorable meal. The seasonal mango offerings added a unique touch to the experience. A great spot for enjoying delicious food and innovative seasonal specials in a vibrant setting.

featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Tanatan Juhu recently and loved the whole experience. The ambience is beautiful and the live singing adds such a great vibe. We tried Virgin Sangria, KitKat milkshake, veg platter, Kakhra with avocado dip, and main course dishes like paneer makhani, dal bukhara with lachha paratha and stuffed kulcha with pindi chole – everything was very tasty. Ended with a delicious gulkand cheesecake. Great place for good food and amazing ambience

featured_reviews.name: Mommy OnDuty
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the most mesmerising place that we have visited recently. What to say what ambience and food. Service is super efficient and food is super delicious. Has Visited with my family and loved the food . We had spiked sikangi and sharvi kava in cocktails and I must say spiked sikhangi is a must when visiting here. In starters we has zafrani tangi and kebabs which were delicious. A special mention to the ambience and live retro music made my evening. The artist was very melodious. Loved the singing. Overall the experience was a 5* . There are lot of restaurants in Juhu but Tanatan is different . U will love the whole package here be it food , ambience, staff service . Really made my day. Will visit again soon . Highly recommended for a visit here

featured_reviews.name: Avni Barai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had such a lovely dinner at Tanatan, Juhu last night with friends! The vibe was great, but the food honestly stole the show.

We started with the Avocado Thecha—a super unique twist with just the right balance of creamy and spicy. The Zucchini Paneer Roll was another standout, really fresh and flavourful.

The Firangi Nuska was interesting and well-executed, and the Tandoori Butter Roti paired perfectly with the comforting Dal Khichdi—simple, but done so well.

For drinks, Anar Ka Pyaar was refreshing and not overly sweet. And desserts were a total highlight—Killer Kit Kat was indulgent and fun, while the Rajasthani Ghevar added a nice traditional touch to end the meal.

Overall, a great mix of innovative and comforting dishes. Definitely a place I’d come back to!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Hatiskar
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing dining experience at Tanatan where the ambience instantly sets the mood with classy interiors, warm lighting, and soothing live music that makes the evening feel special and lively at the same time. We started with the Bhuna Chaap which was smoky, flavorful, and perfectly cooked with tender texture in every bite. The Murg Bharwaan Lahori was rich and indulgent with delicious stuffing and a creamy gravy that had bold authentic flavors. The Lucknowi Nihari stood out with its deep aromatic taste and slow cooked meat that was extremely soft and full of spices. The Chicken Biryani was fragrant and well layered with balanced flavors and juicy chicken pieces that made it very satisfying. Cheese Garlic Naan was soft, buttery, and generously filled with cheese, pairing beautifully with the gravies. The cocktails Penicillin and South Side were refreshing and well crafted, one offering smoky citrus notes and the other giving a light minty freshness that complemented the food perfectly. We ended the meal with Rasgulla Tiramisu which was a unique fusion dessert combining soft rasgulla with creamy tiramisu layers creating a delightful balance of flavors. Overall the food quality, presentation, service, and live music made it a complete and memorable experience.

I had a fantastic experience here! The food was quite delicious, but the bar program really stands out—the cocktails are crafted with fresh seasonal fruit and are exceptionally well-balanced.
The highlight of the night was definitely the Baklava. The presentation was stunning; it was served with rose petals dried right at the table using dry ice, creating a beautiful theatrical effect. It tasted as good as it looked! Highly recommended for anyone looking for great flavors and a bit of "wow" factor.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute is one of the best Middle Eastern restaurants if you are looking for authentic flavours, beautiful presentation, and a relaxed dining experience. The food arrives as a visual treat, and every dish feels thoughtfully prepared with a balance of spices and textures that reflect Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine.

We started with refreshing mocktails like the Green Avocado and the Salted Caramel Baklava Sheikh, followed by the classic Bayroute Muhammara — smoky, nutty, and addictive. The Shrimp Provencal was juicy and perfectly spiced, while the Chelow Kebab with rice stood out for its simplicity and flavour. The Moroccan Lemon Olive Chicken was tender, aromatic, and comforting.

To end the meal, the Chocolate Kunafa was crispy, gooey, and indulgent. The warm lighting, elegant interiors, and calm ambience make Bayroute ideal for date nights, family dinners, or relaxed evenings with friends. If you are searching for a premium Middle Eastern dining experience, Bayroute is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: shravan saroj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute in Juhu offers a spectacular culinary journey across the Middle East. The ambiance is luxurious and elegant, making it perfect for a special occasion.
They specialize in authentic Turkish, Lebanese, and Mediterranean cuisine. Their menu features a delightful array of classics, all prepared with finesse.
A must-try is the signature hummus—creamy and flavorful—along with the perfectly flaky Baklava. The 'Egyptian Photo' cocktail is highly popular for its unique, Instagram-worthy presentation.
While the food quality and presentation are exceptional, the service can sometimes be a little slow. Despite this, the attentive and polite staff ensure a pleasant dining experience. It remains a top recommendation for those seeking a truly authentic and high-end taste of the Levant in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Vipasha Pillai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dinner at Bayroute with my mom recently was a fantastic experience, especially since it was our first visit here. The restaurant impressed us instantly with its tasteful interiors and calming ambience, making it ideal for a relaxed dinner. The service complemented the setting beautifully. Thanks to Shadab, who was taking care of our table. He was attentive and helped us with spot-on recommendations.
.
Here's everything we tried (Highly Recommend):
1. Sumac De-light: A beautifully balanced cocktail with half vodka and half gin. It was refreshing and presented beautifully in a glass dome with smoke
2. Rehan: A light and incredibly refreshing mocktail
3. Harissa Chicken Kebab: Chicken was grilled to absolute perfection and served with a unique cream cheese dip
4. Chicken Afrikaan: A signature Pide (Turkish flatbread) dish. It was flavourful and super comforting with just the right amount of spices and chicken chunks
5. Lavash Crust Chicken Kabsa: Soo loved this! It's an aromatic spiced rice dish paired with tender chicken and a crisp lavash layer that added great texture to the dish
6. Baklava: Finally, ended our meal with their signature dessert that was crisp, nutty and indulgently sweet
.
Overall, the food stood out for its depth of flavour with Middle Eastern & Mediterranean influences coming through beautifully in every dish. Everything was well-balanced, well-presented and soo delicious. A special mention for the restaurant manager, Mr. Gautam, whose warm and gracious hospitality added a personal touch to our dining experience 😊
.
Bayroute delivers on every front, be it ambience, food, drinks and service. It's worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Indica Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute is a stunning Middle Eastern restaurant that offers a perfect blend of elegance, comfort, and cultural charm. The moment you step in, the ambiance draws you in with its warm tones, tasteful interiors, and thoughtfully designed spaces that feel both inviting and premium.
The restaurant is spacious with comfortable seating, making it ideal for families, group gatherings, and even intimate date nights. The décor reflects Middle Eastern aesthetics beautifully—subtle, classy, and immersive without being overwhelming.
What truly enhances the experience is the hospitality. The staff is polite, attentive, and extremely accommodating, ensuring everything runs smoothly while making guests feel genuinely welcome. The overall vibe of the restaurant is relaxed yet lively, allowing you to enjoy conversations without any rush.
Bayroute is more than just a restaurant—it’s a place where ambiance, service, and experience come together effortlessly. A great choice for those looking to enjoy a refined dining atmosphere with an international touch.
Highly recommended for anyone seeking a memorable restaurant experience.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

•	Spaghetti Aglio Olio with Pepperoni – Taste was decent, but it was on the drier side.

The staff was friendly and efficient, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. I’d definitely recommend this place for a date night, an evening out with friends, family get-togethers, or even colleague dinners.

Tip: Make a reservation in advance to avoid waiting, and if you’re booking via Zomato, you can also avail 20% off when you pay through the app.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐.

featured_reviews.name: Benjamin SHIH
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my first time visiting India, and I’m so glad we found this gem. The Owner/Chef is incredibly welcoming; he personally helped us order and explained the flavors with such passion.
We are from Taiwan and have tried many top-tier Indian restaurants back home, like Saffron (番紅花), Taj (泰姬), and Mayur (馬友友). But the Gosht Lucknowi Dum Biryani here is on a whole different level. My friend even said it’s 10 times better!
• The Mutton: I’ve never had mutton this tender. It’s perfectly marinated and practically falls apart. You can really taste the "Kung Fu" the Chef puts into the slow-cooking.
• The Sauce: That rich, golden gravy isn't just a sauce; it's a concentration of slow-cooked onions and spices that melt in your mouth.
• The Pro Move: Make sure to mix in the spicy yogurt raita. It cuts through the richness and adds a whole new layer of flavor to the fragrant rice.
If you want a meal made with genuine heart and soul, this is the place. A huge thank you to the Chef for such a warm welcome to India!

featured_reviews.name: shraddha nabar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved the food at The Bombay Curry!

For the 1st time we saw a chef personally taking orders and preparing them for us. We were already in heaven. The moment came when food was served it was mind blowing.

We had chicken Angara , Chicken Malai kebab, Luckowi Murgh Makhani, Dhaniwal Korma & Hyderabadi dum biryani.
I absolutely loved the chicken angara starter. Easily one of the best, juiciest and most succulent chicken I’ve ever had. Not to forget the Hyderabad biryani and Dhaniwal Korma Soooo good!

Also had a lovely conversation with Chef Kunal Nagpal and got to know about his story and how he started the restaurant.
Food, ambience, staff-  Awesome, definitely recommended

featured_reviews.name: Kaivan Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very popular kebab & biryani restaurant just next to Khar station West.
It is very small joint with about five small tables.
It is air-conditioned but a little cramped to sit.
If tables are occupied then be prepared to wait for a table.
Service is also a bit slow as everything is freshly prepared after order is taken.
Food is their positive point.
The owner is friendly & sitting at counter.
The chef moves around & takes the order.
We tried chicken raezala kebabs which were fresh & tasty with tandoori rotis.
Also tried the gohst Lucknowi dum biryani which was also good but taste was not as per our expectations.
On the whole a good place to visit if in Khar area.

featured_reviews.name: Sunny Solanki
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our first meal in Mumbai turned out to be an absolute gem! 🍽️
We visited a small restaurant with a cozy sitting area that can accommodate around 10 people, but the food was truly 1001%.

We started with two types of kebabs — super tasty, juicy, and full of flavor 🤤. Then came the curry with fresh naan, and everything was prepared fresh and served hot. You can really taste the quality and effort in every bite.

Small place, big flavors! 💯
Really enjoyed our first meal in Mumbai and would definitely recommend this hidden gem to anyone looking for authentic, freshly prepared food.

featured_reviews.name: Shreeya Mehrotra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a North Indian living in Mumbai, and everyone knows that Mumbai doesn’t really do good North Indian food unless it’s fancy. Most days you just adjust, but some days you really miss proper food. That’s exactly the kind of day I found Bombay Curry and honestly I’m so glad I did. This place feels so homely. It’s the kind of place you go to on a random night when you’ve had a bad day, you’re tired and you just want something that feels like home.

We ordered butter chicken, garlic naan and seekh kebab and every single thing was a straight 10/10. The butter chicken was rich and comforting, the garlic naan was soft and perfect and the seekh kebabs were juicy and full of flavour.

What makes it even more special is knowing that the chefs are from Lucknow and Rajasthan because you can genuinely taste that authenticity in the food. And the chef/owner himself was easily one of the most friendly and nicest chefs I’ve ever met. Warm, welcoming and clearly cooking with a lot of love. Bombay Curry feels like a hug on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar “Sagar Anil” A
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience was an 80–20 mix, but overall quite memorable. We’ve visited multiple restaurants across Mumbai and often seen chefs deeply occupied with their cooking schedules. Here, however, we met Chef Kunal Nagpal—a chef with a story, beautifully balancing restaurant management and creating magic with his food.

We reached the hotel around 3:45 PM, just before closing time, which meant our order was taken in a bit of a hurry. We patiently waited for the food, and that’s where the experience truly took a turn for the better.

We ordered Chicken Malai Tikka and Butter Chicken, and both dishes were outstanding. The masala was rich and delicious. A special recommendation: do try their Chicken Malai Tikka—it’s a must!

Overall rating: 8/10. If you’re a fan of Mughlai chicken, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

Chef, we wish you continued success and all the best for your future endeavours.

Thank you,
Sagar & Tejashree

Everyone will agree that Beeji ki Rasoi is always tasty & made with loads of love 😜

Beeji ki Rasoi is special for every kid, so when I saw there is a delivery kitchen named after one - I couldn’t resist & ordered some food last night to try it out.

For people who don’t know :- Beeji in punjabi means mom or grand mother.

My Veg Order was as follows :-
Veg Kadhai Dhaba
* Veg Kadhai subzi - Tasty
* Chole Masala subzi - Delicious
* Dal Makhani - Simply irresistible
* Steam Rice - Perfectly Cooked
* Sheera ( dessert ) - My favourite
* Chapati ( 4 of them ) - Soft

Note :- All Dhaba’s contain 4 chapatis, Bhaji, Black Dal, Rice, Meetha, Salad, Onion, Sprout & Pickle.

Cheese Chilli Paratha
The cheese & chilli stuffing was spicy & pretty heavy so order accordingly.
It blended beautifully with Chole &
Dal Makhani. I personally prefer Paratha / Naan over chapati or Rotis with my
North Indian Curries.

Beeji ki Rasoi lives up to its famous tag line & offers Customised packaging, great food quality & decent quantity ensuring our order is sufficient for 2 eaters.
If you don’t stay with your beeji or family members - after eating from beeji ki Rasoi you’ll definitely remember your family 😍

All in all a great place to order delicious home style North Indian food 🥘

Aloo paratha

Loved the place and holds true to the name.

Overall I loved the food! It's was filling and light on stomach. Just like home food.
Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Golden Wave Restaurant in Santacruz, Mumbai, for dinner with family and friends. The restaurant has a pleasant ambience with comfortable seating and a relaxed atmosphere, making it a good place for an evening meal.

We started our dinner with the Chicken Tandoori, which was well-marinated, nicely cooked, and packed with authentic smoky flavors. The chicken was tender and served fresh, making it the highlight of our meal. For the main course, we ordered the Mutton Dum Biryani. The biryani had aromatic rice and flavorful spices, while the mutton was cooked well and complemented the dish nicely.

However, the overall dining experience was affected by a couple of drawbacks. The service was noticeably slow, and we had to wait longer than expected for our food to arrive. While the quality and taste of the dishes were satisfactory, the portion sizes felt quite small considering the prices charged. This made the meal seem less value-for-money than we had anticipated.

That said, the restaurant's ambience and the taste of the food were enjoyable enough to make the visit worthwhile. If the management improves the speed of service and offers more generous portions, the overall experience would be significantly better.

Overall, Golden Wave Restaurant offers decent food in a pleasant setting, but there is room for improvement in service efficiency and portion sizes. I would rate my experience 3 out of 5 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Utekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambiance of the restaurant is really good and creates a pleasant dining atmosphere. However, the food experience was average considering the price range.
The service was decent and staff were polite, but a couple of dishes didn’t meet expectations. The Chicken Chilly and Achari Paneer Masala were noticeably more salty than usual. The Achari Paneer lacked the expected tangy flavour and tasted saltier instead.
That said, the food was not bad overall. The Chicken Tikka, Veg Spring Rolls, and Masala Soda were quite good and enjoyable.
Overall, it was an average dining experience compared to what I was expecting. The place has great ambiance and potential, but some improvement in taste balance and consistency would make the experience much better.

featured_reviews.name: Ms.Dear369
featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.review_text:
Randomly got recommendation. Thought of giving it a try. I was pleasantly surprised. Its a newly opened restaurant with authentic Punjabi dishes. Real good service from the staff. Firoz gave us good recommendations and was really helpful and courteous. Will recommend this place for its cozy vibes and great food.

Dish recommendations

Paneer Tikka starter - delicious
Paneer Butter masala combo - just the right flavors
Lassi - Excellent

PS. A review was requested by the staff and they provided complimentary desert. I was gonna give them a 5star review anyway because it was such a good experience. I would recommend patrons to check out dine in offers on popular apps like district and Swiggy dineout for discounts on the total bill.

featured_reviews.name: Rahil Kotadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.name: Suhani Mendonsa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar just got a delicious new reason to celebrate with Bawa Kitchen opening its doors this Lohri! From the first bite, it felt like a true Punjabi feast — rich, soulful and full of festive warmth. My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!
And yes, my festive Lohri fit was specially curated — can’t wait to share it with you all soon!

featured_reviews.name: Susheel Dharmani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Bawa Kitchen and had a good dining experience overall. The place has a simple yet comfortable ambience, perfect for a relaxed meal.
The food quality was nice, especially the North Indian dishes which were flavorful and well-prepared. Portion sizes were decent and prices felt reasonable for the location.
Service was quick and the staff was polite and attentive. It’s a convenient option if you’re staying nearby or looking for a reliable place to eat in Dadar.
Overall, a good spot for a casual meal with consistent quality.

featured_reviews.name: Jawahar Hingorani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I only gave 4 for atmosphere because there was no 4.5 or 4.75…and I got bitten by mosquitoes! The food was on point - I ordered Ajwaini Rawas for my appetizer and it came with this spicy tandoori salad (think Thai Som Yum but not as sweet or wet) and Green chutney which was the perfect accompaniment. For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Vijita Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text: The Bawa Kitchen delivered a great dining experience—pure Punjabi vibes, full balle-balle. The ambience is lively and authentic, with vibrant cut-outs and the iconic “Khatiya” as a standout photo spot. Veg and non-veg starters are well curated and set the right tone for the meal. Special mention to Rahul for being an excellent host—his food suggestions and positive approach added real value to the experience. Overall, a visit that is absolutely worth it for good food, warm hospitality, and Punjabi flair.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. The Karam Podi Dosa is your usual slick dosa, but with Karam Podi masala which was too spicy for me. The Pesarattu, a healthy moong dal dosa, was perfect though. I really enjoyed it. Another of their healthy offerings is the Millet Cone Idli, served in this very cute manner. It is plain and pasty, and a must try. All of this comes with 4 chutneys, each with their own kick. What you can’t miss here at all is their Filter Kaapi Soft Serve - it’s like creamy cold coffee. So good. Overall, this place offers unique and healthy options, so if that’s what you like, check it out.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

featured_reviews.name: Vardhita Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overall, the experience was okay, but they definitely need to work on their management. It was quite crowded, and the person handling it wasn’t able to manage things well. Plus, the kiosk machine for ordering and payment wasn’t working, which made it a bit inconvenient.
Food Feedback:
1) Karam Podi Dosa – Felt dry and was served cold.
2) Ghee Podi Idli – Hardly any podi, and the idli was way too soft — almost like it wasn’t cooked properly.
3) Millet Cone Idli – Nice and different, but they can totally skip the ice-cream stick.
4) Filter Kaapi – Tasted good, but sugar should be on the table. We had to ask twice before we got it.
5) Chutney – Would be great if they could increase the quantity a bit.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am so in love with Andhra cuisine — those soft, soft idlis and dosas are my absolute weakness! I recently visited a new place that opened in Bandra, and it’s perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
The food here is pure bliss. The chutney, the sambhar — the authenticity is just amazing. The millet cone idli was my favourite!
We also tried their Ghee Podi Idli and Button Vada — so fresh and so yummy, I just couldn’t say no.
The Karam Masala Dosa was nice and crispy, and the Poori Saagu was absolutely ultimate.
Overall, the food is superb and I truly enjoyed every bit of it.
And lastly… Filter Coffee is a must before you wrap up your meal.
Do check this place out if you’re an idli fan just like me!
They have limited menu but super tasty 🤤

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Mommy OnDuty
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice cozy ambience with awesome south indian food. All dishes tastes delicious and is priced appropriate for the pocket. Dont forget to try its Karam podi dosa, andhra style poori sagu, ghee dosa with authentic filter coffee….

featured_reviews.name: 1TeaspoonLove
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nanna house is an Andhra style kitchen serving authentic Andhra food.
Small place, small menu but big on flavour.

The dishes are served with 4 types of chutneys and sambar.

The idlis were super soft almost melted in the mouth. We loved the Babai idli which were dipped in ghee topped with white butter. So good! The podi idli was good too.

We tried the Karam podi and pesarattu .. both were crisp and tasted good. The karam podi was garlicky and spicy.

We also tried the cone ragi idli which were decent.

The filter coffee was good but the filter coffee soft serve was excellent. Must try. It was smooth creamy and perfect.

Overall good food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Follow me on Instagram for more details
@kapaianita

A slice of Andhra in the heart of Bandra West 🤍
A newly opened South Indian spot in Bandra West bringing honest, homestyle Andhra flavours to the table — perfect for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

Some must-trys from the menu:
• Ghee Podi Idli — soft idlis tossed in fragrant podi with a generous drizzle of ghee.
• Babai Idli — pillowy idlis dunked in ghee and topped with butter… pure comfort.
• Millet Cone Idli — a healthier, cone-shaped twist on a classic.
• Pesarattu — crispy, savoury moong-dal dosa packed with herbs and flavour.
• Karam Podi Masala Dosa — a spicy Andhra-style dosa with a bold kick.

If you’re chasing simple, soulful, South Indian food — this place is highly recommended. 🌿✨

featured_reviews.name: Sadhana Viswanadhuni
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a true Hyderabadi my search for such amazing biryani never ends! I hated mumbai for not having it here! But now I don't need to look any further😍😍😍
Biryani By Kilo's biryani are sooo hyderabadi in taste that one is definitely going to have a foodgasm!❤️
My search ends here today as now I'm gonna keep ordering from BBK to satisfy my biryani cravings 😍😍 We ordered for
Paneer Nawabi Curry ✨
A delectable paneer dish! The gravy was very smooth with the right amount of spices and softtt paneer 😍
Ulte Tawa ka Parantha ✨
It's like a thicker smaller version of rumali roti but much better than that! As we ordered the food earlier we heated it up on tawa and savoured it with the paneer curry 😍
Veg Hyderabadi Biryani ✨
A properly packed flavoured rice with amazingly marinated veggies! The masalas were right and yummm. What more?? They even serve it with SALAN like in Hyderabad!!!!! 😍😍😍💞
Veg Kathal Dum Biryani ✨ - MUST HAVE!!!!!!!
This delicacy of south is a seasonal favourite and I was very doubtful if it would match to my expectations and mind me it was way beyond that! It had the perfect taste like we get it back in south!
And it was a super hit with all my family members!
😍😍😍
The biryanis were served with
Onion and lemon salad
Salan and Raita too❤️

Coming to the packaging can you think of any other better eco friendly packaging?? To top it off they even provided us with an aanch lighting which allows one to place the pot on candle burner! Which is sure to keep the handi and rice in it warm and fresh😍😍😍

If the green dough sealing gets hard and tough to remove! Don't hesitate to take help of a knife! That part might be tricky but I think a good sealed bowl is very important for perfect biryani 😍🤤🤤

So happy to have stumbled upon this brand! Forever thankful for bringing Hyderabadi Biryani to Mumbai 😍😍😍😍😍😍😍

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani by Kilo is one of safest and trusted brand delivering quality biryanis to our doorstep.
Last Thursday we ordered some of the dishes from there. The best thing about them was they deliver biryanis in earthen pots.
Delivery was quick and on time.
The dishes we tried were :

1) Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani (5/5) : Served in a earthen pot with live heating candles. The rice was cooked well. Chicken pieces were perfectly coojed in spices. Overall the biryani was awesome.
Salan and raita was complementary with the biryani was so good.

2) Chicken Korma (5/5) : It was lil sweet as I love. Chicken cooked in thick gravy had lipsmacking flavours. It was also packed in earthern pot.

3) Ulte Tawa ka Paratha (5/5) : It was just perfect. I was trying this first time and really love it.

All the dishes were scrumptious and enough for 3 people .
Hygine and stromg packing was done to avoid spillage and contamination.
Proper safety checks were done.

They made my day, surely gonna order them again.

featured_reviews.name: Foodie Kudi ke Chatake
featured_reviews.review_text: Are you a biryani lover ? If yes then Biryani by kilo is what you should try must. Very impressed with their matka packing which is being offered with candle and a mud pot to heat thir biryani before having it. Secondly packing was excellent and food delivered was peeping hot. Also there is a chutney served along with biryani which is a perfect combination to have with their biryani. Paneer nawabi was good in taste specially the paneer pieces were very soft. Overall a good first experience with them. Will surely try their other varieties in Biryani specially.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Kwatra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Best Biryani ever! I love Biryani by Kilo. They have the longest, most flavourful rice in their Biryani. We love their Hyderabadi Biryani the most. It is spicy and made in masalas. It comes with delicious salan, onions and green chutney. The chicken in the biryani is nice and juicy and quantity is also quite good. The handi has to be heated for 5-7 mins before having it. It is Highly recommended to do so as it gives steamy hot well done rice in your plate and it feels we are at a restaurant.
We also had chicken korma with ulta tawa parathas. Korma was also delicious and had quite authentic taste and flavor. The paratha when heated on tawa became nice and flaky. Suggest you to do the same but not too much as it becomes too crisp.
Overall Excellent food delivery and always trustworthy for the taste and flavor. Value for money!

featured_reviews.name: A P
featured_reviews.review_text: We had lunch at Khane Khas at Bandra west today. First thing I noticed is that the owner Mr Chaddha gave me a warm smile as soon we entered. We started off with Aam panna- made fresh by Mr Chaddha’s mother who is 85 years of age. Perfect taste and quite refreshing. We started with MUTTON SEEKH ROLL. Juicy & tasty mutton kebab in a roll. (5/5). Then we had PUNJABI MUTTON SUKKA ( thick gravy with tender flavorful pieces of mutton - the spices were underplayed perfectly to enhance the flavor of mutton, exactly how I like it) - 5/5. The only dish which did not meet up to our expectations was the Dhuan paneer masala. The paneer was quite soft and tasty but the taste of the gravy was not put the mark. But all of that was overshadowed by the attitude and demeanor of Mr Hardeep Singh Chaddha- - very warm & humble. ( he even allowed us take a picture with him) Thanks for a great experience and will surely come back to try other dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Parimal Udapurkar
featured_reviews.review_text: This place had hands down the best service I have experienced in Mumbai. In addition to the great food, the plates were spotless, the serving of lachha pyaaz was generous, the water was served a perfect cold and the waiting staff was attentive and prompt. These things don't happen on their own without someone's attention to detail. Incredibly lucky to have dined at a place run so passionately.

featured_reviews.name: akshat singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Quite a decent restaurant to try out good north indian food. Their spice levels are good and the masala's are used in just the right quantity making the dishes delectable and sumptuous. Their tandoori is absolutely heart-warming but the dhuan chicken was not worth the hype it has.

Ambience is not too great but on a cool windy day, it's a good place. The staff is really polite and helpful. Worth a try outlet for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera

Khane khas is one of those small warm places you go to in bandra for a hot desi meal.
My friend tried the dal tadka that was perfectly made, just enough for us to be  to be able to alter it to our preferences.
The butter chicken they have is just the way I like it, non sweet. It's savoury and delectable.
The garlic naan and kulcha both were nice as well. All in all a good hearty dinner.

featured_reviews.name: HASJIV SINGH ANAND
featured_reviews.review_text: Despite having an enormous menu, I’d suggest you stick to their Indian cuisine, particularly the fish dishes. The Rawas Tikka is made up of soft, juicy well cooked fish pieces rubbed in a delicious tikka masala, slightly spicy & sour. I could eat just the gravy, it's that good 🌝- thick, a little coconutty but without the strong aftertaste. The red curry is spicy but also not too sharply flavoured in any single direction. There was a phase 🌜where I tried fish fingers from every restaurant in Bandra in search of my childhood nostalgia. If you're in Bandra, this is one of the best places to assuage the craving. First off they serve a huge quantity of fingers, easily shared by two people. The batter is slightly thick but not very oily, so you actually get to taste the fish which is flavourful and lightly spiced. Chips are an added bonus.

featured_reviews.name: Rekha Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
We are cured here in the restaurant. We called the restaurant to book table and were told quite abruptly that no bookings will be accepted and if we are lucky and come right away we may get a table. So we reached within the next 25 minutes and found a table. The person asked if I had a booking and I looked at him pointedly and said that I was told table was by luck and not booking!
However, there was only one person authorised to take orders where we were seated and he was incharge of 8 tables. Which meant one had to wait for that one person to get free to place order.
The waiting staff seemed cordial, but the manager staff were abrupt and had a chip on their shoulder.
The food arrived in reasonable time. And it was okay, nothing extraordinary, but not bad too.
We ordered for dessert and that again came in reasonable time, again nothing extraordinary. The rabdi we ordered was sour, but the senior intervened immediately and had that changed. He seemed to be the only one concerned about the guests here!
All in all, given it is Christmas, some good cheer, and making a guest feel special would have made the experience more enjoyable.
I for sure will not consider this place as my first option if I have to bring over friends , largely due to the abrupt behaviour.

featured_reviews.name: Preeti S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani is a favourite Indian cuisine. Its basically a perfect balance of spices & rice.
'Go Biryan' is a newly opened joint in Khar which promises to make some best "Biryani's with Dum" surely stand true here.

I called for the following items

Chicken Afgani Tikka Biryani - this had an irresistible aroma of saffron , caramelized onions and afgani chicken tikka pcs. Portion quantity is sufficient for one person and had accompaniments like laccha onions & raita. Chicken pcs were soft & tender and perfectly marinated in spices. Tasted Good

Paneer Tikka Vegetable Biryani - This smelled great when i opened the box, it had mild fragrance of indian spices (Garam masala), vegetables cooked in masala along with some pieces of paneer tikka. This also came along with Raita & onions. I found it to be on a bit oilier side.

Classic Chicken Tikka - Boneless pcs of chicken marinated in spices and cooked in a tandoor  accompanied with green chutney...It had the classic tandoori flavour which one would want in chicken tikka.

Divine Chocolate Mousse - scrumptious!!

Overall all both the biryani's were delectable and easy on my pockets!!

My only suggestion t the management - containers for raita and salad can be made more sturdier as by the time they arrive, the cardboard lid becomes too soggy and messy to handle !!
